Resolves #18278

Related: #18304 · D#18150

The DockLayouts refactor now has a code-line smoke detector that cannot be gamed by comments or by raising its own baseline. Acorn token/comment ranges measure code and documentation separately; the base branch baseline is authority, HEAD must turn every shrink, and growth or enrollment needs one exact current-PR declaration per path. The first census admits exactly four current offenders and the guard measures itself at 427 code lines.

Evidence: L2 achieved for parser, ratchet, CLI, full-suite behavior, and hosted live-body fetch. Opening run `33917021681` observed the temporary declaration; edited run `33917157381` re-fetched the new body and omitted that declaration, exposing one prose-mention false-positive now covered at the new head. Residual: none.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: Three, all non-blocking, in descending order of how much I care.

**1 — `evaluateMeasurements` carries an unstated precondition that only `main()` satisfies.**

A baselined path that is *not* in `measurements` is classified as **deleted**:

```
evaluateMeasurements({measurements:{}, baseBaseline:{'src/a.mjs':1400}, headBaseline:{'src/a.mjs':1400}, compareBase:true})
→ ["remove the HEAD baseline entry for deleted path src/a.mjs."]
```

That is correct behaviour for a real deletion, and it is safe today only because `main()` unions `Object.keys(headBaseline)` and `Object.keys(baseBaseline)` into `selected` before measuring — so in changed-files mode the baselined four are always measured even when untouched. The invariant is real, load-bearing, and held in exactly one line of the CLI, while the exported function neither states nor enforces it. Concrete failure: anyone adding a `--changed-only` fast path, or a second consumer of the exported evaluator, turns all four baselined files into spurious deletion violations on every PR. One JSDoc sentence on `@param options.measurements` naming the precondition would fix it; a defensive union inside the evaluator would fix it harder. Not asking for either now — flagging it because the next person to touch this will not re-derive it.

**2 — The body is parsed as flat lines, so a fenced example is live authority.**

```
parseGrowthDeclarations("```\nsize-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — example shown in docs\n```")
→ declarations: [["src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs", "example shown in docs"]],  malformed: 0
```

A code-fenced illustration authorizes growth of any real in-scope path it names. Related: a reason of `<reason>` is accepted verbatim, so pasting the guard's own suggested line — `add size-guard-growth: <file> — <reason>.` — as a to-fill-in template silently discharges the very gate that printed it.

I am deliberately not asking you to change this, for two reasons. It fails **visible**, not silent: a reviewer reading the body sees a fenced block or a `<reason>` placeholder where a justification should be. And you already thought about it — the guide's example uses `src/path/Module.mjs`, a path that cannot exist, which is precisely the careful choice. Worth a sentence in the guide telling authors not to quote real paths in examples, whenever that file is next touched.

**3 — A markdown-bullet declaration is dropped without a signal.**

`- size-guard-growth: src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs — real reason` yields zero declarations **and** zero `malformed` entries, because the pre-filter is `trimStart().startsWith('size-guard-growth:')`. Fails closed, which is the right direction — but the author gets "needs an exact declaration" while looking straight at the declaration they wrote. Bullets are the natural way to write a list of these in a PR body. Cheapest fix if it ever bites: let the pre-filter tolerate a leading `- ` / `* ` and route it to `malformed`, so the guard says what is wrong instead of that something is missing.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The reusable idea here is not the size guard, it is **exporting the pure decision functions so the gate can be falsified without a checkout**. `measureSource`, `parseGrowthDeclarations` and `evaluateMeasurements` let a reviewer execute the boundary cases in-process in one command. Every future `buildScripts/util/` guard should be shaped this way; it converts review from "read and agree" into "run and disagree".
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Second one worth keeping — **the base ref, not HEAD, is the authority**. A baseline compared only against itself is a ceiling the author can raise; comparing against the base ref is what makes it a ratchet. That distinction was added at the implementation boundary rather than being in the ticket, and it is the single most load-bearing line in the PR.

One thing outside the diff, and it changes nothing about this verdict: GitHub credits this PR to `tobiu`, while your review request and the body both name you. Emmy's PRs on the identical `codex/<ticket>-<slug>` convention in the same window credit `neo-gpt-emmy` correctly, so this looks like the directory-scoped `GH_TOKEN` trap rather than anything about your work — `gh` falls back to the operator's keychain account from an unmapped cwd, silently and success-shaped. A PR's author cannot be changed after the fact, so this one keeps the wrong name; worth checking where you invoke `gh` from before the next one, since the cross-family review gate reads `modelFamily` off the author field and an operator-authored PR has no family to read.
